# IT Applications in Business and Commerce

## Read this first — the course title is misleading

**This repository is not business analytics.** There is no e-commerce model, CRM, ERP, supply-chain
simulation, payment system, market-basket analysis, RFM segmentation, forecasting model or KPI
dashboard anywhere in the code. A reader arriving from the course title will expect the opposite of
what is here.

What is actually in the tree is two unrelated deliverables:

| Unit | What it is | Stack |
|---|---|---|
| `project/` — **AI Racer** | a [[proximal-policy-optimisation]] agent driving in TORCS over the [[torcs-scr-protocol]], for the IBM AI Racing League | Python + [[pytorch]] |
| `lecture/exam_prep/` — **IT Apps Knowledge Test** | a zero-build single-page quiz app, 497 questions across 28 sets | vanilla HTML/CSS/JS |

Business-systems material — SOA, BPEL, BPMN, WSDL, SOAP, REST/microservices, virtualization, PKI,
proof-of-work — appears **only as quiz content** in `chapters.js`. Not one line of code in this repo
implements a business system. Tagging the AI-Racer material `business-systems` would misfile the
whole repo, so none of these pages carry that tag.

**Status: coursework, finished and frozen at last commit 2026-07-25.** "All finished and frozen"
(interview, 2026-07-28). Nothing here is maintained.

## The git history is a publication record, not a development record

11 commits, ~100 tracked files, ~9.8k lines of Python and JS, ~25 MB of committed binaries. **Eight
of the eleven commits land inside six seconds** on 2026-07-10T20:46, importing a complete,
documented, screenshot-illustrated tree. A second micro-burst on 2026-07-25 changes **36 lines
total** and touches no code. This is the cleanest instance of [[import-finished-work-into-git]] in
the corpus, with the polish tail of [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]] — with one inversion worth
recording: licence work is commit **#1** here, not the last act.

**The real development history lives in a different repository.** `Szymon1905/AI_racer_pytorch`,
six named authors, branch tips dated 2026-04-19 → 2026-06-17. None of that history is in this git.
Commit messages here are uniformly publication-facing ("Add the top-level guide…", "Remove
decorative emoji…"); **none describes a bug, an experiment or a decision** — the exact opposite of
the messages quoted *inside* the branch reports.

`project/docs/branch-reports/` — 11 markdown files, 846 lines — is a mechanical branch-by-branch
audit of that other repository, with tip SHAs, constants tables, reward pseudocode and a lineage
graph. See [[generated-audit-artifact]] and [[branch-per-experiment]]. **Its generator was never
committed**, so unlike the sibling instances of that pattern the audit cannot be re-run.

The table pairs full names with institutional student identifiers. **This wiki deliberately omits

The blanket `publish: false` on this repo's pages was lifted on 2026-07-30. **The omission was

these files at all, so there is nothing for a publish flag to hold back. Re-checked on 2026-07-30
against person-like values across every page resting on this repo; `audit-secrets` re-checks the
published subset on every build. What goes public is the engineering: the [[torcs-scr-protocol]]
client, the generated question bank, the branch strategy.

## `guide.txt` — a documentation-drift showcase

Four distinct failures in one file, all instances of [[documentation-drift]]:

1. The banner stamps the focus track as corkscrew while §0, §3.1, §3.5 and G8 still target
   **alpine-1** and save to `lines/alpine-1.npz`.
2. §8 lists `gym_torcs/recon_lap.py`, and gotchas G4/G5 plus validation V4 depend on it — **the file
   does not exist**.
3. §1 describes the *pre-rewrite* baseline (steer-only, gear hardcoded to 1, 23-dim state) as "What
   exists today", contradicting the shipped three-dimensional-action racing-line environment.
4. §7 proposes a speed-cap curriculum that nothing in `train_torcs_rl.py` implements.

Seven further drift instances exist elsewhere — a stale copy-pasted `commands.txt`, a report claiming
12 log files where 9 exist, `eval_torcs.py` for `eval_torcs_rl.py`, Obsidian wikilinks that render as
literal brackets on GitHub, and a top-level README that softens a failure the branch's own README
states flatly.

**The last commit in the repo exists solely to remove a pointer to agent tooling.** As committed on
2026-07-10, `guide.txt` opened with:

> "architecture in this repo. Read CLAUDE.md first for the project map; this file"
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/code/a.bhuiyan/guide.txt, 2026-07-10

`439a690` (2026-07-25T02:04) rewrites that line to point at the README instead. No `CLAUDE.md`,
`.claude/` or `AGENTS.md` exists in the tree **or in history**. Agent tooling was present in the
working copy and deliberately excluded from publication — the repo's final act was scrubbing its last

## The exam-prep app, and where the lineage starts

`lecture/exam_prep/` is the **origin** of the four-repo exam-prep lineage:

> "One was first and I copied it forward."
> — interview, 2026-07-28

The user names this repo as the first. One caveat is recorded rather than dropped: the earliest
*in-repo* mtime evidence points at `Physics/exam_prep/` instead (2026-06-27→06-30), and this app has
no comparable in-repo timestamp because its development history lives in the other repository. See
[[course-as-runnable-study-tool]], [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] and
[[offline-first-static-deliverable]].

The app itself is the strongest engineering in the repo: all scores **derived** from the `answered`
set rather than kept in desyncable counters, `STORAGE_VERSION = 7` invalidation, and `qa_test.js` —
a hand-rolled `node:vm` + DOM-shim harness that loads the *production* `app.js`, drives real event
handlers and **exits non-zero on failure**. It is the only automated test in the repo;
`_smoke.py` prints and never asserts.

**Content provenance, stated because no README states it.** The 20 study sets are a **synthetic**
bank — disclosed only in a code comment in `_build_bank.js`, never in any README, while the root
README says the app "turns the whole syllabus into an interactive quiz". The 8 "Testownik" sets are
**real past-exam questions** whose primary source (`uploads/Quiz_Question_Bank.md`) is absent from
the repo.

- **TODO:** the copyright status of the Testownik question source is unestablished and the primary
  files are missing, so their answer-key verification is unauditable. **No quiz item is reproduced
  in this wiki**, and none should be. `confidence: low` on any provenance claim for that bank.

The training CSVs are clean by contrast: 9 files, 330 rows, machine-written by this repo's own code
against a simulator on 2026-06-04/05. No personal or commercial data.
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] is unusually well done here — `.gitignore` explains *why*
the ~1 GB TORCS simulator is excluded, `NOTICE` attributes the upstream work, the README has an
explicit "Not included:" callout, and `a.bhuiyan/README.md` lists five failures by track coordinate.
